issues.text: Outline item 1 says a meeting without purpose/output/note 'is a conversation, which is fine but shorter'. The lesson keeps only the negative half ('a conversation that leaves nothing behind'); the 'fine, but shorter' qualifier is not established anywhere, and misconception 3 pushes further the other way.
issues.quote: Without them it is a conversation that leaves nothing behind.
issues.fix: In §4, after 'A meeting costs everyone in the room at once…', add one clause: 'Talking without a decision is fine; it just does not need a meeting's time box — keep it short.' No other change.

issues.text: Unconditional 'has to be asked again': an unwritten question is not necessarily re-asked; claim 17 is opinion with no evidence, so the wording should be hedged like the rest of the lesson.
issues.quote: a question nobody wrote down has to be asked again, often in another meeting
issues.fix: Replace with: 'a question nobody wrote down usually gets asked again, often in another meeting.' Mirror in quiz q4 explanation.correct (en/vi).

issues.quote: Name what you want decided — which state the refused order gets — not the area it is about, and say what you do if no answer comes today.
issues.text: The two rules for a good message (name the decision, not the topic; say your default if nobody answers) first appear here, in Try it. Section 4 only says a question with one owner is cheaper in writing. I can still do the exercise because the step spells them out, but quiz q4 option c leans on the same rule and I only knew it from Try it.
issues.fix: In section 4, after 'the answer stays where the next person looks.', add one sentence: a written question works when it names what has to be decided and what you will do if no answer comes.

issues.quote: The next person is you, and what reaches you is the file, not the conversation.
issues.text: Section 4 talks about 'the note' in general, then suddenly says 'the file'. I had to go back to the situation to see it means docs/team/meeting-notes-example.md.
issues.fix: Replace 'the file' with 'the note' (or 'the written page') in that sentence.

issues.quote: The note is written for the team, in Vietnamese, on one page; everything described next sits above the lines quoted below.
issues.text: I re-read this twice: 'everything described next' covers only the next two paragraphs (Mục đích … Lý do), but the fourth paragraph (Việc phải làm) describes the quoted table itself, so for a moment I thought I had missed a block.
issues.fix: Say 'the next two paragraphs describe the part of the file above the lines quoted below'.

issues.quote: of the three lines, the blocked one survives the crossing out, often as the only one.
issues.text: If nothing blocks me right now, my 'blocked' line is 'nothing', and the expected result does not tell me whether that counts as success or means I did it wrong.
issues.fix: Add a short clause: if nothing blocks you, write 'nothing' on that line; then 'next' is the line to keep only if someone waits on it.
